numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Casting a datetime64/timedelta64 SparseArray with a datetimelike fill_value to an integer or boolean Sparse dtype resolves the target fill to the subtype default (0/False) instead of converting the source fill, so every unstored position densifies to the wrong value; e.g. arr.astype("Sparse[int64]").to_dense() gives [0, 0, 1451779200000000000] while arr.to_dense().astype("int64") gives [1451692800000000000, 1451692800000000000, 1451779200000000000]. Also, sparse.astype("Sparse[int64]") on a NaT-containing array yields Fill: 0 rather than raising.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The source fill_value should be converted to the target subtype, so the densified result matches the dense conversion: [1451692800000000000, 1451692800000000000, 1451779200000000000] for the PR#68463 reproducer; for NaT fills, converting should raise ValueError ('Cannot convert NaT values to integer') consistent with dense astype.
trigger_conditions: SparseArray with datetime64[ns] or timedelta64 subtype (kind 'M' or 'm')
fill_value is a datetimelike scalar such as pd.Timestamp, pd.Timedelta, pd.NaT, or unit-less np.datetime64('NaT')
astype to an integer or boolean Sparse dtype whose fill_value equals the default (0/False)
Under the pre-fix code, a fully-stored or NaT-fill path also affected the result

input_output_examples.input: vals = np.array(["2016-01-02", "2016-01-02", "2016-01-03"], dtype="M8[ns]"); arr = SparseArray(vals, fill_value=pd.Timestamp("2016-01-02")); arr.astype("Sparse[int64]").to_dense()
dti = pd.date_range("2016-01-01", periods=3); ser = pd.Series(dti); ser[0] = pd.NaT; sparse = pd.core.arrays.SparseArray(ser.values); sparse.astype("Sparse[int64]")
input_output_examples.expected_output: Fill should be converted from NaT rather than becoming 0; converting the NaT fill to integer should raise ValueError ('Cannot convert NaT values to integer'), matching dense.astype('int64')
